children: and cut a fiber-optic cable in New Jersey, knocking out a backup connection after a separate primary circuit failed at a Federal Aviation Administration air traffic facility.

In a statement, Verizon said the cable runs along the Amtrak rail line in New Jersey and that its technicians were working to repair it. The FAA had discovered that the backup fiber line was cut after the primary circuit carrying data into the Philadelphia facility failed.

The communications problems disrupted flights across the U.S. Northeast, with the FAA temporarily halting some incoming flights at Philadelphia, Newark Liberty, and Teterboro airports. The disruption also affected JFK and LaGuardia, while some flights began resuming at LaGuardia and Philadelphia by early afternoon.
More than 600 flights at Newark and Philadelphia had been delayed, according to FlightAware, while Newark delays averaged 112 minutes. Newark is a major United Airlines
hub, and Philadelphia is a major American Airlines

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said the agency was installing a new circuit on the primary line while working to repair the backup fiber. He estimated the fiber break could take about 13 hours to repair.
The primary circuit is due to be replaced as part of an overhaul of the nation's air-traffic-control system.

title: Verizon says contractor cut fiber cable amid Northeast flight disruptions
